tldr: The TornadoVM team presents jitLLM, a pure-Java GPU inference engine that mixes TornadoVM-generated CUDA kernels with NVIDIA libraries inside CUDA graphs to reach 90%+ of llama.cpp decode throughput.
summary: Michalis Papadimitriou and Orion Papadakis opened with a demo on an RTX 4090: a Java inference engine running Qwen3 4B in FP16 generated TornadoVM Java code for a Mandelbrot kernel, which a tool-calling harness compiled to CUDA and ran on the same GPU. The project, last year called GPULlama3.java, is now jitLLM. They claimed it reaches 90-97% of llama.cpp decode throughput and sometimes beats it on prefill, across models such as Gemma 4, GLM 4.7 and a 27B Qwen. A year ago they were 10-30x slower. They pitched it as the GPU option for local inference that stays in Java, alongside CPU-only projects like Llama3.java and JLama.

Papadimitriou summarised TornadoVM as a Java GPU programming framework for JDK 21 to 27, now on Maven and SDKMAN, with four programming levels: @Parallel loops, the low-level KernelContext API, a newer tile-based API, and library tasks that call NVIDIA libraries such as cuBLAS, cuDNN and cuFFT directly. Papadakis then walked through jitLLM's layers: a public API (load a GGUF, open a session, generate), an engine that queues and schedules requests for experimental continuous batching, a models layer for families, quantizations (FP32, Q8, Q4) and execution modes, abstract operation 'programs', a lowering step to TornadoVM task graphs, and a backend SPI choosing GPU or CPU. A paged KV cache shares blocks across sessions.

A live benchmark used a Java port of llama.cpp's own bench harness (4K-token prefill, 128-token decode, five repetitions) on Qwen3 0.6B: prefill was 1.2x llama.cpp, decode 93%. The gains come from mixing operators per layer. Model-specific steps like RMSNorm and RoPE use JIT-compiled TornadoVM kernels, compute-bound matrix multiplications in prefill go to cuBLAS, and the whole sequence is captured as a single CUDA graph to avoid per-kernel dispatch. Decode is memory-bound, so it stays fully JIT. Batch prefill gave 15x over token-by-token, and native libraries added more on top.

jitLLM plugs in three ways: its Java API directly, as a model provider for Quarkus LangChain4j, LangChain4j or Spring AI via application properties, or as an HTTP server with 'jitllm serve'. Demos ran the Quarkus LangChain4j weather sample (three tools: extract city, geocode, forecast) and a GitHub pull-request reviewer on a 27B Qwen model. The reviewer was pointed at a real jitLLM PR and at a draft PR porting Quarkus LangChain4j to Quarkus 4. The team plans to add the reviewer to its CI.
keyPoints: jitLLM (formerly GPULlama3.java) is a Java LLM inference engine that compiles model layers to CUDA via TornadoVM at runtime.
On a Java port of llama.cpp's benchmark harness, they reported prefill at 1.2x llama.cpp and decode at 93% for Qwen3 0.6B, with decode above 90% on larger models.
TornadoVM library tasks call cuBLAS, cuDNN, cuFFT and CUTLASS from Java without JNI, and chain them with generated kernels in one task graph.
Each transformer layer becomes one CUDA graph mixing JIT kernels and cuBLAS calls, so it is dispatched once instead of per operation.
Prefill is compute-bound and benefits from vendor libraries; decode is memory-bound and runs best as fully JIT-compiled kernels.
The layered design (API, engine, models, programs, lowering, backend SPI) supports FP16, Q8 and Q4 quantization, a paged KV cache and experimental continuous batching.
Integration is via a Java API, a Quarkus LangChain4j / LangChain4j / Spring AI provider, or a local HTTP server started with jitllm serve.
takeaways: Install TornadoVM through SDKMAN and run the jitLLM Quarkus demos on your own NVIDIA GPU.
If you run local models through llama.cpp or Ollama from Java, benchmark jitLLM as an in-JVM alternative for your models.
When optimising GPU pipelines, use vendor libraries for compute-bound steps and custom kernels for memory-bound or model-specific ones, and capture the sequence in a graph.
Open issues on the jitLLM project for models or LangChain4j features you need; the team asked for them.

quotes.text: If you're having a project that runs on llama.cpp, you can swap it with jitLLM and you can get roughly 90% to 97% the same performance in throughput.
Let's just use this NVIDIA library, they've been solving this problem for two decades now. We cannot do better.

watchIf: You want to run local LLMs on NVIDIA GPUs from Java without JNI or a Python sidecar, or you are curious how inference engines squeeze performance out of a GPU.
